messages:
jessica.support: Customer (Acme) reports they get a 429 mid-stream, client reconnects and receives duplicate partial tokens charged. They sent ledger rows showing +350 tokens then another +320 for same user and same original stream_id. Request ids: r_3fa2 and r_3fa2-resume. Can we triage? :grimacing:

mike.client-eng: ack. Can you paste the raw client sequence? Are they rotating the Authorization header on reconnect?

jessica.support: yes, they rotate tokens. Steps they gave: 1) start SSE with token T_A 2) after ~12s server returns 429 and closes 3) client exchanges creds, gets T_B 4) client reconnects with T_B and includes Last-Event-ID header containing last_event_id=482. Response resumed but includes repeated chunk at id 480-482. Ledger shows charges for both streams.

dan.oncall: do we have request ids for both attempts? you mentioned r_3fa2 and r_3fa2-resume — are those correlated server-side?

jessica.support: attaching snippets (redacted):

```
# client request (first attempt)
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer T_A
Accept: text/event-stream
X-Client-Stream-ID: s_987
```

```
# server log (first)
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] req=r_3fa2 stream=s_987 user=acct_acme tokens_consumed=350 status=429 reason=rate_limit midstream
```

```
# reconnect
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer T_B
Accept: text/event-stream
Last-Event-ID: 482
X-Client-Stream-ID: s_987
```

```
# server log (resume)
[2026-03-12T14:02:26Z] req=r_3fa2-resume stream=s_987 user=acct_acme tokens_consumed=320 status=200 resume=true
```

jessica.support: ledger rows: both r_3fa2 and r_3fa2-resume show charges to acct_acme. Customer says they should only be charged for unique tokens beyond last confirmed event.

alex.devex: interesting — they rotated auth and used Last-Event-ID. Our resume code path currently attributes token_usage to the incoming bearer token (T_B) and creates a new request entry rather than attaching resumed tokens to original req id. That will show up as two separate charges if both entries are billed.

ingrid.billing: confirmed: billing table indexes by request_id and auth_token_hash. If resume creates new request id, token attribution goes to new token. We do have a reconciliation job that tries to dedupe by stream_id but it only runs nightly; customer wants immediate rollback.

mike.client-eng: reproducer idea: send a short stream, then trigger rate limit with a low quota account, then reconnect with rotated token while sending Last-Event-ID. I can try locally. Any headers we should include to help server attach to original session?

jessica.support: they already sent X-Client-Stream-ID. server logs show stream=s_987 in both entries. Seems race between rate-limiter returning 429 and audit layer committing a partial token charge.

sre-bot: diag hint: check rate-limiter window and whether midstream 429 triggers finalize_billing(true) call. If we finalize early, tokens are marked billed for that request id.

mike.client-eng: repro steps I ran:
```
# quick repro script (simplified)
1) start stream with curl SSE and token T_A
2) flood with high-per-token prompt to hit quota in 10s
3) when server returns 429, rotate token and reconnect with Last-Event-ID
```
I see duplicate payload for last chunk and two billing entries locally.

alex.devex: root cause hypothesis: resume path creates new billing_record and doesn't check for original_billing_record when Last-Event-ID provided. Should instead try to attribute resumed tokens to original request if stream_id matches or if original request still has in-flight billing.

ingrid.billing: mitigation options: 1) manually revert the second billing_row for acct_acme (quick but manual), 2) run dedupe reconciliation job now for stream s_987, 3) change billing policy to bill only on stream finalization (requires broader change). Which do we want?

dan.oncall: immediate: do (2) run dedupe for s_987 and refund duplicate. Also add customer-facing note and credit. Longer term: engineering to change attribution logic.

mike.client-eng: for engineering fix: I'll open an issue. Fix should: when resume request includes X-Client-Stream-ID or Last-Event-ID, attempt a bind to original billing record if its state is PENDING and the time window < 60s. If original is already finalized, don't attach. Also add a metric for "resume_rebind_fail" so billing can monitor.

alex.devex: agree. Also add server header on 429 responses: `X-Stream-Terminal: true|maybe` to indicate whether client should attempt resume vs restart. For now, we should mark midstream 429s as terminal if rate-limiter is the cause (so clients will start fresh and not double-bill).

jessica.support: customer asked for ETA and immediate credit. Ingrid will do the refund. Can we estimate engineering turnaround?

mike.client-eng: I'll do a patch to attribution logic in the next sprint; hotfix possible if we accept small risk. ETA for hotfix: 48-72h. Full solution in next release cycle.

ingrid.billing: processed interim credit of 670 tokens to acct_acme (ref: credit-1976543210-acct_acme). I'll follow up with invoice note.

jessica.support: thanks team — looping in customer with status. We'll follow up after mike's patch. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: reminder: open postmortem if multiple customers affected.

jessica.support: filing internal ticket: INF-7129 (resume-billing-attribution).
